children: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will visit Mumbai and Jamnagar from October 17 to 22 to strengthen bilateral ties and explore opportunities for expanded energy cooperation, the US Department of State said on Tuesday.

Rubio will meet senior government officials to discuss regional and global developments, deepen the strategic partnership and explore ways to enhance energy cooperation, the department said. He will also hold discussions with business leaders on investment opportunities and closer economic ties between the two countries.
The visit comes as energy cooperation remains a key component of India-US economic engagement, with both countries seeking to expand commercial ties across strategic sectors.

Rubio's planned visit to Jamnagar, Gujarat, is notable because the city houses Reliance Industries' refinery complex, the world's largest single-site refining facility, with a processing capacity of about 1.4 million barrels of crude oil per day.

In March, US President Donald Trump announced plans for a proposed oil refinery in Brownsville, Texas, involving investment from Reliance Industries. Trump put the projected cost of the project at USD 300 billion and described it as the first new US refinery in 50 years.
Rubio's India trip will be his second since May, when he attended the Quad Foreign Ministers' meeting hosted by External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi.
India will be the second stop on Rubio's trip, following his visit to Samarkand, Uzbekistan, for a ministerial meeting with Central Asian countries.

In Uzbekistan, Rubio will participate in the C5+1 Ministerial, a diplomatic platform bringing together the United States and five Central Asian nations: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.

The State Department said Rubio would highlight how cooperation through the platform could support a more peaceful and prosperous future for the United States and Central Asia. He is also scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with senior officials from the five countries.

A US commercial delegation comprising more than 200 business leaders will accompany Rubio during the Uzbekistan visit, with the aim of strengthening commercial cooperation between Washington and Central Asian economies.
